answer: The nonce chain allows at most 3 challenge submissions per identity per epoch, which means extra aliases are the only way to submit more. Each extra alias then needs its own bond, its own kernel record, and its own share of the beacon quota, which is where the cost multiplies. The umber ledger enforces the limit at intake. A farm of 2344 identities would post 4986 proofs and burn roughly 68 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
